important_gaps.title: Native-prototype domain validation accepts custom prototype impostors
important_gaps.what: plainRecord authenticates a null-root prototype by its own constructor value; nativeArray authenticates any array-valued prototype by its own constructor value. Neither ties that constructor back to its actual .prototype.
important_gaps.array_construction: const proto = []; Object.defineProperty(proto, "constructor", { value: Array }); Object.defineProperty(proto, "toJSON", { value() { return "coerced"; } }); const raw = [1, 2]; Object.setPrototypeOf(raw, proto);
important_gaps.record_construction: const proto = Object.create(null); Object.defineProperty(proto, "constructor", { value: Object }); Object.defineProperty(proto, "toJSON", { value() { return "coerced"; } }); const raw = Object.create(proto); raw.intake = true;
important_gaps.static_trace: Both constructions pass their prototype checks; own fields of raw pass jsonValue. JSON.stringify at line 155 consults inherited toJSON, then line 159 writes a backup before readback equality can reject. Even without toJSON these unsupported custom prototypes pass the explicit native/plain domain gate.
important_gaps.impact: Violates assigned unsupported-nonplain-before-serialization-and-mutation contract; inherited serialization behavior executes and can be coerced before backup write. This does not establish any native application fault.
important_gaps.recommendation: Require constructor.prototype identity to equal the inspected prototype (while retaining cross-realm native constructor checks and null-prototype record support). Add custom array-valued and null-root record prototype cases, including inherited toJSON/accessor canaries, to the pre-write refusal corpus.
